text: Lesson 1's Ops ask: see how many orders are sitting in each status, so you know where orders are piling up. That's a count, by status, on fct_orders.

Order Count uses distinctcount of order_id, not countrows of fct_orders. If fct_orders ever has more than one row for the same order_id, for any reason, a plain row count would silently inflate right along with it. Distinctcount stays correct regardless. Keep this in mind.
The required visual: status on the axis, Order Count as the value, using the real status values recorded back in Lesson 1 — placed, shipped, completed, returned.
Orders Stuck counts orders that aren't completed and were placed more than seven days ago — a real operational tripwire Ops can check daily, not just a status breakdown.
Next lesson: a test fails, now what. A real dbt gotcha — a join fanout — and the method for diagnosing it starts here.
